$comment: Golden base: the pinned system and modules a rebuilt Foundry install needs.
"Always latest" is the documented hazard, not the goal (see docs/PROJECT.md on
foundry-mcp module/server drift). Move a pin with
`node scripts/content/foundry-base.mjs update`, review the diff, commit it.
Ids and versions came from `foundry-base.mjs capture` against a live world,
never from guesswork: six of the eight original placeholders were wrong in
ways no amount of care would have caught — Chat Commander is "_chatcommands",
Prime Performance is "fvtt-perf-optim", Dice Tray is "dice-calculator", and
Argon is two modules rather than one.
manifest URLs were filled from the capture files via:
node scripts/content/foundry-base.mjs promote foundry-capture-<world>.json
A pin without a manifest URL is reported by `provision`, never guessed at.
Two fields carry behaviour beyond the version:
coupled - this pin is half of a fact that lives in two places, so `update`
holds it out of a batch and names it. Move it by asking for it by
id, together with its other half, in its own change.
check   - a deliberately floating URL, used ONLY to ask what is current. A
version-locked manifest URL serves its own version forever, so a
locked pin without a check URL is invisible to the watcher.
Every pin that can be is version-locked: the manifest URL names the exact tag
a rebuild installs, and a floating `check` URL sits beside it so the pin stays
visible to `update`. Before this, 22 URLs ended in /releases/latest/ or a branch
tip, so `provision` installed whatever was current and wrote that back — a
record of what happened, not a constraint on what will. The 2026-08-21 drill
proved it: nine pins installed at versions nobody chose.
`update` moves a locked pin's URL and its version together, and reports rather
than half-moves a pin whose URL it cannot rewrite. The four gitlab.com pins
stay floating on purpose: that host is not on the devcontainer firewall
allowlist, so a locked tag URL cannot be verified from here. Each says so.

core.coupled: MCP_VERSION in scripts/setup-mcp.sh is the other half. The module and the server are one fact, and a batch bump would move one of them.
core.note: Pin must stay in step with MCP_VERSION in scripts/setup-mcp.sh — the module and the server are one fact. Version-locked to the v0.8.2 tag rather than master, because master served 0.8.3 during a rebuild and would have put the module ahead of the server with nothing saying so. `update` will report this pin current forever; move it by editing the tag in the URL, the version here, and MCP_VERSION together, then re-run scripts/setup-mcp.sh. The `download` is pinned too, and has to be: the v0.8.2 manifest points its own download at /releases/latest/, so locking the manifest alone read 0.8.2 and installed 0.8.3.
core.title: Foundry MCP Bridge

core.note: Version-locked to the 6.1.1 tag; `check` reads the master tip, which is where this module publishes without cutting release assets.
core.title: Universal Battlemap Importer

core.note: The only automated path for player characters, and D&D Beyond is their source of truth. Nothing else in the pipeline needs it — statblocks come from the vault via the SRD caches, scenes from dd-import, journals from obsidian-bridge — so it earns its pin on PCs alone. It is also the most expensive pin: a live D&D Beyond session cookie in world settings (the reason world-capture redacts credentials at all), twelve world-scoped world.ddb-* packs that die with the world, and therefore a full munch re-run as step 7 of every rebuild. Kept anyway: re-typing a party of sheets per session costs more than one re-run per rebuild, and rebuilds are rare while sessions are not. Version-locked to the 7.4.2 release tag: the module also publishes under a rolling tag named literally `latest`, which is what the `check` URL reads.
core.title: D&D Beyond Importer
